---
type: memory
title: Exponent Rules
---

Flip two cards at a time. Match each **expression** to its **simplified form**.

| Expression | Simplified |
|:-----------|:-----------|
| $x^a \cdot x^b$ | $x^{a+b}$ |
| $\frac{x^a}{x^b}$ | $x^{a-b}$ |
| $(x^a)^b$ | $x^{ab}$ |
| $(xy)^a$ | $x^a y^a$ |
| $x^0$ | $1$ |
| $x^{-a}$ | $\frac{1}{x^a}$ |

## Hint
Write it out the long way. $x^2 \cdot x^3 = (x \cdot x)(x \cdot x \cdot x)$: count the $x$'s.

## Hint
Multiplying powers **adds** the exponents, and dividing **subtracts** them. A power of a power **multiplies** them.
A negative exponent means "flip it into a fraction", not "make it negative".

## Solution
Each rule comes from counting factors. For example, $(x^2)^3 = x^2 \cdot x^2 \cdot x^2 = x^{2+2+2} = x^6$, so a power of a power multiplies the exponents.
